'''Anne J. McNeil''' (born June 17, 1977) is an American chemist who currently works at the [[University of Michigan]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://lsa.umich.edu/chem/people/faculty/ajmcneil.html|website=University of Michigan Chemistry Faculty|title=Anne McNeil Faculty Profile|access-date=27 January 2018}}</ref> where she holds the position of [[Arthur F. Thurnau]] Professor of Chemistry and Macromolecular Science and Engineering. In 2017, McNeil was named a [[Fellow of the American Association for the Advancement of Science|fellow]] of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] (AAAS).<ref>{{cite news|last1=Erickson|first1=Jim|title=Seven U-M scientists, engineers named 2017 AAAS Fellows|url=http://ns.umich.edu/new/releases/25268-seven-u-m-scientists-engineers-named-2017-aaas-fellows|access-date=28 January 2018|agency=University of Michigan|publisher=Michigan News|date=20 November 2017}}</ref>

==Biography==
McNeil is from [[Buffalo, New York]]. She graduated from the [[College of William & Mary]] in 1999 with a Bachelor of Science in chemistry. Her graduate work was with Dave Collum at [[Cornell University]], studying the aggregation [[Chemical kinetics|kinetics]] and chemistry of [[lithium amide]]s and lithium [[enolate]]s. After earning her PhD in chemistry in 2005, McNeil was a post-doc with [[Timothy M. Swager]] at [[MIT]] from 2005 to 2007, studying [[conjugated polymer]]s.<ref name="hhmi">{{cite web|url=http://www.hhmi.org/scientists/anne-j-mcneil|website=Howard Hughes Medical Institute|title=Anne J. McNeil, PhD|access-date=27 March 2018}}</ref> She now has two kids and a dog named

She joined the faculty of the [[University of Michigan]] in 2007 as an assistant professor of Chemistry and Macromolecular Science and Engineering. She became an Arthur F. Thurnau professor in September 2013, and a professor for the [[Howard Hughes Medical Institute]] in 2014.<ref name="hhmi"/>

==Scientific career==
McNeil's lab at the University of Michigan is known for providing mechanistic understanding to the [[catalyst transfer polymerization]] process, helping to show that the likely intermediate is a catalyst-polymer π-complex,<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Bryan|first1=Zachary|last2=McNeil|first2=Anne|title=Conjugated Polymer Synthesis via Catalyst-Transfer Polycondensation (CTP): Mechanism, Scope, and Applications|journal=Macromolecules|date=3 September 2013|volume=46|issue=21|page=8395 |doi=10.1021/ma401314x|bibcode=2013MaMol..46.8395B |url=http://mcneilgroup.chem.lsa.umich.edu/wp-content/uploads/2015/05/Macromolecules_2013_8395.pdf|access-date=28 January 2018}}</ref> but the lab has a diverse focus.

For her work on [[Conjugated system|conjugated]] polymers, there has been considerable focus on expanding the use of catalyst transfer polymerization to make polymers of novel or hard-to-reach architectures (such as conjugated [[gradient copolymer]]s<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Palermo|first1=Edmund|last2=McNeil|first2=Anne|title=Impact of Copolymer Sequence on Solid-State Properties for Random, Gradient and Block Copolymers containing Thiophene and Selenophene|journal=Macromolecules|date=20 July 2018|volume=45|issue=15|pages=5948–5955|doi=10.1021/ma301135n|url=http://mcneilgroup.chem.lsa.umich.edu/wp-content/uploads/2015/05/Macromolecules_2012_5948.pdf|access-date=28 January 2018}}</ref> or insulating-conducting block copolymers<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Souther|first1=Kendra|last2=Leone|first2=Amanda|last3=Vitek|first3=Andrew|last4=Palermo|first4=Edmund|last5=LaPointte|first5=Anne|last6=Coates|first6=Geoff|last7=Zimmerman|first7=Paul|last8=McNeil|first8=Anne|title=Trials and tribulations of designing multitasking catalysts for olefin/thiophene block copolymerizations|journal=Journal of Polymer Science Part A|date=26 October 2017|volume=56|pages=132–137|doi=10.1002/pola.28885|doi-access=free|hdl=2027.42/139919|hdl-access=free}}</ref>) and for studying the properties of new conjugated polymers<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Smith|first1=Mitchell|last2=Leone|first2=Amanda|last3=Zimmerman|first3=Paul|last4=McNeil|first4=Anne|title=Impact of Preferential π-Binding in Catalyst-Transfer Polycondensation of Thiazole Derivatives|journal=ACS Macro Lett|date= 9 December 2016|volume=5|issue=12|pages=1411–1415|doi=10.1021/acsmacrolett.6b00886|pmid=35651203 }}</ref> or new blends of known polymers in solar cells to improve their performance.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Palermo|first1=Edmund|last2=McNeil|first2=Anne|title=Impact of p-conjugated gradient sequence copolymers on polymer blend morphology|journal=Polymer Chemistry|date=26 June 2013|volume=4|issue=17|pages=4604–4611 |doi=10.1039/c3py00601h|url=http://mcneilgroup.chem.lsa.umich.edu/wp-content/uploads/2015/05/Polym_Chem_2013_4606.pdf|access-date=28 January 2018}}</ref>

Another focus has been on molecular [[gelation]]; McNeil has published molecular [[gels]] as sensors of many harmful or hard to detect compounds. This is with the underlying assumption that it is easier to determine if a gel has formed (since it will go from a flowing solution to a gel that resists flow) rather than alternatives, such as if a solution has changed color (which can be difficult to discern if the analyte is strongly colored). McNeil's lab has produced gel-based sensors for [[Mercury (element)|mercury]] ions,<ref>{{cite journal|last1=King|first1=Kelsey|last2=McNeil|first2=Anne|title=Streamlined approach to a new gelator: inspiration from solid-state interactions for a mercury-induced gelation|journal=Chemical Communications|date=1 March 2010|volume=46|issue=20|pages=3511–3513|doi=10.1039/c002081h|pmid=20582351|url=http://mcneilgroup.chem.lsa.umich.edu/wp-content/uploads/2015/05/Chem_Commun_2010_3511.pdf|access-date=28 January 2018}}</ref> [[nitrite]] ions,<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Zurcher|first1=Danielle|last2=Adhia|first2=Yash|last3=Dı´az Romero|first3=Julian|last4=McNeil|first4=Anne|title=Modifying a known gelator scaffold for nitrite detection†|journal=Chemical Communications|date=2014-05-27|volume=50|issue=58|pages=7813–7816|doi=10.1039/c4cc02504k|pmid=24905176|url=http://mcneilgroup.chem.lsa.umich.edu/wp-content/uploads/2015/05/Chem_Commun_2014_7813.pdf|access-date=28 January 2018}}</ref> explosives,<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Chen|first1=Jing|last2=Wu|first2=Weiwei|last3=McNeil|first3=Anne|title=Detecting a peroxide-based explosive via molecular gelation|journal=ChemComm|date=26 May 2012|volume=48|issue=58|pages=7310–7312|doi=10.1039/c2cc33486k|pmid=22711139|url=http://mcneilgroup.chem.lsa.umich.edu/wp-content/uploads/2015/05/Chem_Commun_2012_7310.pdf|access-date=28 January 2018}}</ref> [[enzyme]]s,<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Bremmer|first1=Steven|last2=McNeil|first2=Anne|last3=Soellner|first3=Matthew|title=Enzyme-triggered gelation: targeting proteases with internal cleavage sites|journal=ChemComm|date=18 December 2013|volume=50|issue=14|pages=1691–1693|doi=10.1039/c3cc48132h|pmid=24394494|url=http://mcneilgroup.chem.lsa.umich.edu/wp-content/uploads/2015/05/Chem_Commun_2014_1691.pdf|access-date=28 January 2018|pmc=4143987}}</ref> and [[lead]] ions,<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Veits|first1=Gesine|last2=Carter|first2=Kelsey|last3=Cox|first3=Sarah|last4=McNeil|first4=Anne|title=Developing a Gel-Based Sensor Using Crystal Morphology Prediction|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|date=2 September 2017|volume=138|issue=37|pages=12228–12233|doi=10.1021/jacs.6b06269|pmid=27598826}}</ref> which gel when the analyte is present. Many of the gels outperform current sensors for the same materials in sensitivity and in accuracy.

==Awards==
McNeil was one of the first class of Beckman Scholars, receiving an award from the Arnold and Mabel Beckman Foundation in 1998.<ref>{{cite news |title=A Conversation with Dr. Anne McNeil: Celebrating 20 Years of Beckman Scholars |url=http://www.beckman-foundation.org/beckman-news/mcneil-20yearsofscholars |access-date=1 August 2018 |work=Beckman News |agency=Arnold and Mabel Beckman Foundation |date=May 18, 2017}}</ref>  McNeil was also selected for a [[Beckman Young Investigators Award]] in 2009.<ref>{{cite news |title=Anne McNeil |url=http://www.beckman-foundation.org/beckman-young-investigators/anne-mcneil |access-date=1 August 2018 |work=Arnold and Mabel Beckman Foundation |date=2009}}</ref>
